accuracy.evidence: Definitions checked against the AQA and OCR A level Chemistry specifications and the RSC: stationary phase (water bound in cellulose for paper; silica/alumina for TLC), mobile phase (solvent), separation by relative affinity (partition on paper, adsorption on TLC), Rf = spot distance ÷ solvent-front distance from the origin, 0 ≤ Rf ≤ 1, Rf depends on solvent, stationary phase and temperature, pure substance gives one spot, ninhydrin and UV for colourless spots, pencil origin, solvent below origin, lid for a saturated atmosphere. Lab numbers recomputed: 2.0/8.0 = 0.25, 4.4/8.0 = 0.55, 6.0/8.0 = 0.75; challenge 3.6/9.0 = 0.40. Dye Rf values are labelled illustrative in the data file. Parameterised answers (r/100, r·f/100, k/10, n−k) are exact to 2 d.p. and checked at range corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented student errors: 'lighter/smaller substances move further' instead of weaker attraction to the stationary phase, measuring from the paper edge or to the top of a spot, inverting the ratio (Rf > 1), ink start lines, solvent above the origin, matching by colour, and treating one matching Rf as proof. Each has a lab miss message and a challenge tag (flip, base, big, why, level, same, count, size, flip2, see).

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanism is the phase-partition model and the Rf measurement itself: dyes with visible paper-versus-solvent pull ratings are dragged to the band their balance predicts, a draggable measuring line reads distance from the start line to each spot centre, unknown and reference lanes are compared by Rf with a colour decoy, a tank diagram is repaired fault by fault, and a second-solvent chromatogram appears only when asked for. flagsepar (KS3 sieving, filtering, evaporating) does none of this; lab_distinct gate under 30% against all labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover the affinity rule by placing dyes from their attraction ratings before it is stated as a rule; the measuring task makes them feel that the reading must start at the pencil line and stop at the spot centre (edge readings are rejected with a reason); the identification task's red decoy D shows colour is not identity, and the final task makes them request the second solvent before revealing the result.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'near the start line' for a highly soluble dye, '2.5' for an inverted Rf, and 'Yes, same colour' for identification; the following task disproves each and A.reveal reports the result.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions with fourteen tagged wrong answers, each with a specific correction, e.g. 'Measure both distances from the start line, not from the paper's edge: 3.6 ÷ 9.0 = 0.40' and 'Rf changes with the solvent. What stays the same is that there is only one spot.'

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs define stationary and mobile phase before using them, give the Rf formula with one worked number, and keep sentences short; adult text uses specification terms (partition, adsorption, origin, locating agent). The validator's readability limits (kid ≤ 6.5, adult ≤ 9.5) pass.

no_filler.evidence: Each paragraph carries one idea (two phases, why they separate, Rf with a number, purity and identification); the adult text is specification, lab values and named mistakes. Content gate filler and 12% similarity checks pass.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots of every step and mid-task states: the paper sheet and dye card sit side by side without overlap, lane labels moved clear of the start-line spots, Rf labels sit on white tags clear of guide lines and the right edge, set-up faults have both numbered markers and full-width tiles, and the measuring line has 0.2 cm nudge buttons as well as drag.

accessibility.evidence: Buttons for every action (three bands, Line up/down and Check, U contains A–D, each numbered set-up item, each solvent option); the canvas aria-label reads the dye ratings, the line's distance and the front, every Rf on the plate and the set-up state; walk.cjs found no axe WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme on desktop and iPhone 13.

Royal Society of Chemistry, Paper and thin-layer chromatography practical guidance (pencil origin, solvent below the origin, lidded tank, ninhydrin for amino acids)
